title.value: A Reproducible and Realistic Evaluation of Partial Domain Adaptation Methods
title.justification: The title reflects the focus of the study on Partial Domain Adaptation methods, which are a subset of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation techniques. It emphasizes the reproducible and realistic evaluation aspect of these methods.
title.quote: A Reproducible and Realistic Evaluation of Partial Domain Adaptation Methods

extractions.description: This paper examines the effectiveness of Partial Domain Adaptation (PDA) methods, focusing on realistic evaluations without target labels for model selection. The study evaluates seven PDA algorithms across two datasets and analyzes how different model selection strategies impact performance.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily deals with methodologies for improving Partial Domain Adaptation algorithms in Unsupervised Learning. It evaluates model selection strategies and their impact on accuracies without explicit focus on climate or ecological impacts.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The main goal of this work is to provide a realistic evaluation of PDA methods with the different model selection strategies under a consistent evaluation protocol.

primary_category.justification: After a thorough read, the paper's primary focus remains on evaluating Partial Domain Adaptation methods for unsupervised learning without addressing specific climate or ecological areas.
primary_category.quote: This work, we consider the Partial Domain Adaptation (PDA) variant, where target domain classes form a subset of the source domain classes.

secondary_categories.justification: The content is heavily geared towards unsupervised learning methodologies and model evaluations which are not aligned directly with any sustainable development goals or ecological aspects.
secondary_categories.quote: We evaluate 7 representative PDA algorithms on 2 different real-world datasets using 7 different model selection strategies.

primary_sub_category.justification: No specific sub-category matches the content of this paper as it is firmly rooted in improving unsupervised learning strategies rather than addressing environmental categories.
primary_sub_category.quote: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA) aims at classifying unlabeled target images leveraging source labeled ones.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper only pertains to PCA methodologies and strategies, refraining from any ecological or sustainable pseudo-categorization.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Extensive experiments to study the impact of model selection strategies on the performance of partial domain adaptation methods.

applications.justification: There are no applications discussed in this paper that relate to climate or ecologically-related sustainable development.
applications.quote: In this work, we consider the Partial Domain Adaptation (PDA) variant, where we have extra source classes not present in the target domain.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories in use do not align with the content which is purely about methodological advancements in machine learning for domain adaptation.
new_primary_category.quote: The main goal of this work is to provide a realistic evaluation of PDA methods with the different model selection strategies under a consistent evaluation protocol.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: This paper lacks the aspect necessary to create a new sub-category as it does not directly contribute to sustainable development goals.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Most successful algorithms use model selection strategies that rely on target labels to find the best hyper-parameters and/or models along training.
